description: Query a tabular dataset using DuckDB SQL. Call kb_schema first to see available columns. Results shown to you are capped at 250 rows; when capped the response includes truncated:true and totalRowCount (the full row count) - treat that as the signal to re-run with aggregation. The full result is always available to the user via the CSV download, so never widen a query just to see more rows. For analytical questions (outliers, distributions, totals, averages, min/max, highest/lowest, trends, counts), compute the answer in SQL using aggregation (COUNT, SUM, AVG, STDDEV, PERCENTILE_CONT, MEDIAN, MIN, MAX, GROUP BY) or ORDER BY column DESC/ASC LIMIT n - do not select raw rows and inspect them. For outliers, use statistical thresholds (e.g. values beyond mean +/- 2*STDDEV, or top/bottom percentiles via PERCENTILE_CONT) computed over the full table. Prefer selecting specific columns over SELECT *. After results return, interpret the numbers for the user rather than just restating the table. If a result is truncated, tell the user it was capped and re-run with aggregation for a complete answer.
